questions.q: What are the five categories of change in the summary?
a: Stopping, starting, continuing, less of and more of
Planning, doing, checking, reviewing and resting
Thinking, feeling, acting, reacting and resting
Dreaming, deciding, committing, failing and retrying
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses them to sort the dissatisfiers in your life.

questions.q: What did Beyoncé's Sasha Fierce example show?
a: A persona can unlock confidence in demanding moments
Fame requires hiding your true personality
Alter egos replace the need for practice
Childhood rules should shape your stage presence
questions.why: The overview says she borrowed a stronger mindset for performing.

questions.q: What does the summary recommend doing with destructive emotions?
a: Attribute them to a separate character and detach
Suppress them until they disappear entirely
Analyze them in detail before performing
Share them publicly to reduce their power
questions.why: Lesson 2 says naming them as someone else makes them easier to fight.

questions.q: How do you build your alter ego's identity?
a: Define attributes that match your goal and purpose
Copy a celebrity's habits exactly
List every weakness you want to hide
Let friends choose the character for you
questions.why: Lesson 3 says purpose comes first, then the traits needed to reach it.

questions.q: What is the point of the reading-glasses example?
a: A small ritual can switch on the persona you need
Good eyesight improves focus while studying
Props distract an audience from your nerves
Reading is the fastest way to build confidence
questions.why: Lesson 3 shows how a physical cue can summon your alter ego.
